finding: Test 15 asserts four paths are git-ignored (.tp/run-<base>.json, .tp/runs/, .tp/rounds/, .tp/last_failure-<base>.json) while §10.6 says "The .tp/.gitignore fixture gains three entries" — the test and the invalidation note cannot both be satisfied. Worse, §3.1 introduces a fifth artifact, .tp/locks/run-<base>.lock, which no section marks git-ignored and no test covers, so an implementation passing test 15 still commits lock files.
suggestion: Fix the count in §10.6 to match the enumerated set, and either add .tp/locks/ to the shipped .tp/.gitignore and to test 15 or state explicitly that lock files are not ignored and why.

finding: "The driver decides a unit succeeded from its exit code and from re-reading cycle state" never says whether the two are a conjunction or a disjunction, and no test pins either mixed case. Exit 0 with the durable write absent, and non-zero exit with the durable write present, are both reachable (a harness's exit code "need not carry the inner command's", §5.2). Test 21 implies exit code dominates for exit 2 without a record; test 47 implies the record dominates over exit code; §3.3's table implies the predicate decides. This is the loop's central rule and it is the least pinned claim in the spec — retry counts (test 8), unit-failure (§3.4) and last_failure (§4.2) all hang off it.
suggestion: State the rule as a single decidable sentence, e.g. "a unit succeeded iff its §3.3 predicate holds after the child exits, whatever the exit code; a non-zero exit with the predicate satisfied is still a success and sets no last_failure" (or the conjunction, if that is meant). Add two tests: exit 0 + predicate false, and non-zero exit + predicate true.

finding: The `audit-fix` kind's durable write is "That finding's row is recorded resolved", but no tp command, file or field for an audit-row resolution is named anywhere in the spec. `tp review --resolve` exists and gives `review-resolve` a grounded predicate; the audit side has only `tp audit --record`, which records a round's results, not a per-finding disposition. The implementer must invent both the storage (a new field on the recorded audit row? a separate resolution file?) and the command that writes it, and the oracle must then read that same invented state to emit `audit-fix` units keyed by `role:item_id`.
suggestion: State where an audit finding's resolved state lives and what writes it — e.g. `tp audit --resolve <role:item_id> <disposition>` updating the recorded round row — and state that §4.1's oracle derives `audit-fix` units from unresolved rows of the latest recorded audit round.

finding: §3.3 still claims "That is what lets the Stop hook (§6.2) and the driver's own success test read the same condition", but round 8's repair made the driver's condition "exists and every line parses" while §6.2 describes a hook that "reads $TP_ROUND_DIR/$TP_UNIT_ID.ndjson and $TP_RUN_DIR/$TP_UNIT_SEQ-escalation.json" and blocks only when the unit has "neither its findings file nor an escalation record" — i.e. presence. Test 26 asserts the presence form and test 48 asserts the parse form, so the two are implemented from different definitions and the sameness claim is now false: a role that emits an unparseable file is allowed to stop, then fails the driver's predicate and burns a retry the hook could have prevented.
suggestion: Either state in §6.2 that the hook applies §3.3's full predicate (parse every line, within the 10s budget), or drop the "read the same condition" claim from §3.3 and say explicitly that the hook checks a weaker presence condition and the driver owns the parse check.

finding: Round 8 strengthened the role predicate in §3.3 to "$TP_ROUND_DIR/$TP_UNIT_ID.ndjson exists and every line parses", but §4.1's resume rule was left keyed on existence alone: "next_units omits any role whose findings file already exists in the round directory". Within a run the mismatch is masked by the retry path (§3.1 deletes the file before each attempt), but across runs it is not: a driver death that leaves a role file with an unparseable line means the next run's oracle omits that role, the file is never deleted or regenerated, and the record unit merges it. §8a.4 then either exits 1 forever (no line parsed) or silently undercounts the round (some lines parsed) — exactly the defect 8a.4 exists to remove.
suggestion: State the omission rule in §4.1 with the same predicate as §3.3 — omit a role only when its findings file exists AND every line parses — so a malformed leftover is re-run rather than merged.

finding: The oracle omits a role from next_units on file EXISTENCE ("omits any role whose findings file already exists in the round directory"), while §3.3's durable-write predicate is existence AND every line parsing, and §8a.4 makes --merge exit 1 when an input has content lines none of which parse. The three rules deadlock across runs: a role unit that writes a malformed file exhausts its retries (§3.4 unit-failure) and leaves the malformed file on disk — §3.1 only deletes files for units the oracle DID return. The next tp run's oracle sees the file, omits that role, hands the driver a review-record unit, whose merge now exits 1 by §8a.4 and can never succeed. No unit in the design can delete that file, so an unattended run is stuck in a permanent unit-failure loop needing manual filesystem repair.
suggestion: Make the oracle's 'already present' test the same predicate §3.3 states (exists and every line parses), so a malformed leftover is re-run rather than treated as done; state explicitly that a role whose file fails the predicate is returned in next_units and its file deleted before the attempt.

finding: §3.3 claims the Stop hook and the driver's success test "read the same condition", but the two conditions differ. §3.3's role predicate is "$TP_ROUND_DIR/$TP_UNIT_ID.ndjson exists AND every line parses"; §6.2's hook row is "with neither its findings file nor an escalation record", and the prose only says the hook "reads" the path. Test 26 pins the hook on existence, test 48 pins the driver predicate on parseability, and nothing says which one applies to a role unit that wrote a file with one malformed line — the exact case §8a.4 measured on this spec's round 4. Two engineers write contradictory tests: one asserts the hook blocks on the unparseable file, the other asserts it allows the stop.
suggestion: State the hook's condition in the same words as §3.3's predicate (exists and every line parses), or drop the "same condition" claim in §3.3 and say explicitly that the hook is an existence-only best-effort check while the driver evaluates parseability. Add a test pinning the hook's behaviour on an existing-but-unparseable findings file.

finding: The round-8 split of §8a into 8a.1-8a.5 added a fifth required behaviour (8a.4, dropped-role merge), but the section preamble still reads "Four measured defects in the signals an unattended driver consumes" and still cites only four measurement sources ("spec/0.35.0-candidates.md §1, §3, §7 and §10"). A decomposer counting required behaviours from the preamble drops one subsection, and the citation list gives 8a.4 no measurement source even though its own body quotes a measurement (round 4, 33 findings instead of 45).
suggestion: Change the preamble to "Five measured defects" and add 8a.4's measurement source to the citation list (or state inline that 8a.4's measurement is this spec's own round 4 rather than a candidates section).

finding: Test 15 requires four paths to be git-ignored by the shipped `.tp/.gitignore` (`.tp/run-<base>.json`, `.tp/runs/`, `.tp/rounds/`, `.tp/last_failure-<base>.json`), while §10.6 says the fixture "gains three entries". Neither list covers `.tp/locks/run-<base>.lock` from §3.1, so on the literal reading the run lock file is committed. Two of the four are per-base and therefore need glob forms the spec never writes out.
suggestion: Give the exact literal lines the shipped `.tp/.gitignore` gains (e.g. `run-*.json`, `last_failure-*.json`, `runs/`, `rounds/`, `locks/`), reconcile §10.6's count with test 15, and say whether the lock directory is ignored.

finding: Test 16 says "Each §7 field takes its documented default, accepts both range endpoints, and rejects one step outside each". Two of §7's seven rows have no range endpoints at all (`runner`: "Built-in name or object"; `notify_cmd`: "Any command string"), so the universal quantifier is unsatisfiable for them. And "one step outside" is undefined for the two decimal-dollar fields: for run_max_budget_usd (0-10000) is the rejected value -1, -0.01, 10000.01, or 10001? Two engineers write different boundary tests and both claim conformance.
suggestion: Scope test 16 to the five numeric fields, and pin the decimal granularity explicitly (e.g. "values are compared as decimals; -0.01 and 10000.01 are rejected") so the rejected boundary value is a literal, not a derivation.

finding: Test 37 reads "Every child receives the eight documented environment variables with their documented forms", which round 8's own repair contradicts: §3.1's closing line makes TP_ROUND and TP_ROUND_DIR unset — not empty — when the oracle reports round null, so an implement or decompose child receives six, not eight. Test 46 asserts the exception, leaving two tests that cannot both pass as written. (The count is also loose in the other direction: §5.1 adds TP_UNATTENDED to every child, so nine variables are documented as reaching a round-phase child.)
suggestion: Rewrite test 37 as "Every child receives the six always-present variables plus TP_UNATTENDED, and TP_ROUND/TP_ROUND_DIR additionally in a round-based phase", so it composes with test 46 instead of contradicting it.

finding: §10.6 asserts "no other command's exit codes change outside TP_UNATTENDED=1" apart from the arity change, but §8a.4 changes tp review --merge and tp audit --merge from exit 0 to exit 1 whenever an input file has content lines and none parsed — a command exit-code change outside TP_UNATTENDED. §10.6 also omits the payload-shape assertions this release moves for the same reason it lists tp resume: --merge/--status gain location_clusters (§8a.1) and inputs (§8a.4), and file_summary gains truncated/total_changed (§8a.3).
suggestion: Correct the claim to name the --merge exit-code change as a second deliberate break, and add the merge/status/file_summary payload assertions to the invalidated list with the task that moves them.

finding: §10.6 says "The .tp/.gitignore fixture gains three entries", but test 15 (§10.2) enumerates four paths that must be git-ignored: .tp/run-<base>.json, .tp/runs/, .tp/rounds/ and .tp/last_failure-<base>.json. A fifth new artifact, the run lock at .tp/locks/run-<base>.lock (§3.1), appears in neither list, so the shipped ignore file would leave a per-run lock file tracked.
suggestion: Make the two counts agree and decide .tp/locks/ explicitly: either list five entries in both §10.6 and test 15, or state that .tp/locks/ is already covered by an existing ignore rule.

finding: §10.6 says "The .tp/.gitignore fixture gains three entries", but test 15 now enumerates four ignored paths: .tp/run-<base>.json, .tp/runs/, .tp/rounds/ and .tp/last_failure-<base>.json. .tp/rounds/ is the entry the round-8 move of TP_ROUND_DIR from the run dir to a cycle-keyed dir added, and the invalidation note was not updated with it.
suggestion: Change "three entries" to "four entries" in §10.6, or name the four paths there so the count cannot drift again.

finding: TP_RUN_DIR is pinned as "the absolute path of .tp/runs/$TP_RUN_ID" while TP_ROUND_DIR is given only as ".tp/rounds/<base>/<phase>-r$TP_ROUND" — a repo-relative string. §3.1 covers children ("spawned in the repository root"), but §6.2's Stop hook resolves "$TP_ROUND_DIR/$TP_UNIT_ID.ndjson" and §6.3's agent allowlist names the same path, and neither the hook's working directory nor the allowlist's base is fixed anywhere in the spec. Test 37 asks only that TP_ROUND_DIR be "derived from phase and round", so the ambiguity is not closed by a test either.
suggestion: State that TP_ROUND_DIR is absolute, on the same terms as TP_RUN_DIR, and keep the relative form only as the layout description.

finding: `TP_RUN_DIR` is explicitly "the absolute path of .tp/runs/$TP_RUN_ID", but `TP_ROUND_DIR` is given as `.tp/rounds/<base>/<phase>-r$TP_ROUND` with no statement of whether it is absolute or repo-relative — and test 37 reinforces the gap by asserting "TP_RUN_DIR absolute" while saying only "TP_ROUND_DIR derived from phase and round". The value is consumed by a Stop hook (§6.2) and by an agent write-allowlist (§6.3), neither of which is guaranteed to run with the repository root as cwd, so the two readings are not interchangeable.
suggestion: State TP_ROUND_DIR's form as absolute (matching TP_RUN_DIR) and have test 37 assert filepath.IsAbs on both.

finding: §3.2.2 says the driver "reads one number from the final line of that unit's log" at `spend_key`, but never says what happens when that read fails: the final line is not JSON (a harness that ends with a plain-text banner), the dot path is absent, or the value is not a number. The implementer must guess between recording `spend: null`, failing the attempt, or aborting the run — and the choice is load-bearing, because `cap-budget` accrues from it.
suggestion: Add the failure rule: a final line that is not JSON, a missing `spend_key` path, or a non-numeric value records `spend_usd: null` for that unit, contributes 0 to the accrued total, and is reported once (not per unit) rather than failing the attempt.

finding: "Caps are evaluated between iterations only" and the overshoot allowance is stated for wall-clock and budget, but `cap-units` counts spawned children and an iteration spawns a whole role fan-out at once. With `run_max_units` at 100 and 98 children spawned, an iteration of 5 role units either overshoots to 103 or must be truncated mid-fan-out — and truncating a fan-out changes which roles ran for the round. The spec does not say which.
suggestion: Say explicitly that `cap-units` is checked between iterations like the others and may overshoot by one iteration's unit count, so a role fan-out is never partially spawned — or, if truncation is intended, say how a partial round is recorded.

finding: Log paths are `$TP_RUN_DIR/<seq>-<kind>-<id>.jsonl`, but §3.1 makes an `audit-fix` unit's id `role:item_id` and a `review-resolve`/`decompose` id a spec base name — ids that can contain `:`, `/`, `.` and spaces. No sanitization or escaping rule is given, so the log path for an audit-fix unit is not derivable, `{log_path}` (§3.2.1) is not assertable, and test 17 ("a retried unit gets a fresh log path") can only check inequality rather than the documented form.
suggestion: Pin the transformation from unit id to path segment (e.g. every character outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] becomes `-`), and have test 17 assert the exact log path for an audit-fix unit whose id contains a colon.

finding: The log path is `$TP_RUN_DIR/<seq>-<kind>-<id>.jsonl`, and §3.1 makes an `audit-fix` unit's id the finding's `role:item_id`. `item_id` is auditor-authored free text, so it can contain `/`, spaces, `:` or `..`; interpolating it into a filename yields a path that either fails to open or escapes `$TP_RUN_DIR`. The escalation record path is `seq`-based and safe, but the log path and `{log_path}` placeholder are not.
suggestion: Specify a sanitization rule for the id component of the log path (e.g. replace every character outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` with `-` and truncate to a stated length), and state that the sanitized form is what `{log_path}` and the run-state `log_path` carry.

finding: `tp run --status` is specified for a current or last run, and `run_state` covers `stopped`/`in_flight`/`crashed`, but nothing says what `--status` does when `.tp/run-<base>.json` does not exist — no run has ever been started for this task file. Test 14 enumerates only in-flight, converged and stopped. An unattended operator's first diagnostic call hits exactly that state, and its exit code (0 with an empty payload? 1? 3?) is unpinned.
suggestion: Add one sentence giving the no-run payload and exit code, and extend test 14 with the never-run case.

finding: §3.5 requires that both run-state writes be atomic (temp + rename) "because concurrent siblings write rows in the same iteration", but test 12 only checks one row's null exit_code before and its update after — a single-unit assertion that passes against a non-atomic implementation. The property the sentence exists to protect (N concurrent role units each append a row and each update it in place, with all N rows present and none lost) is asserted nowhere.
suggestion: Add a test that runs a full parallel role fan-out through the seam and asserts the run state holds one row per role with every exit_code and duration filled in.

finding: §3.5 requires tp run --status to print "phase" and, on an audit-phase stop, spec_coverage_clean_rounds, role_streaks and divergence, but the run-state JSON schema immediately above it has no field for phase and none for the three signals, and the section also declares the file "observability, not truth" that nothing reads back. After a run has ended, --status must therefore either read the file it says nothing reads back, or re-derive the signals from tp audit --status at report time — which can report a later cycle's values than the ones that were true at the stop §1 promises to explain.
suggestion: Add phase and a stopped-at snapshot of the three divergence signals to the run-state schema and say they are captured at stop time, or state explicitly that --status re-invokes tp audit --status live and that the values are current rather than as-of-stop.

finding: `last_failure` has two writers with no stated ordering: the child, when `tp done` fails the quality gate (the child owns the gate output that `summary` requires), and the driver, when the unit exits non-zero. A gate failure normally produces both, and since "a second failure overwrites it", the driver's generic record can overwrite the informative gate summary that §4.2 explicitly asks for. Concurrent role siblings compound it: two non-zero exits in one iteration both write, with no rule for which survives.
suggestion: Name the writer for each case and the precedence — e.g. the child writes on gate failure and the driver writes only when no record for that `(unit_kind, unit_id)` attempt already exists — and state that writes are atomic and lock-protected, since concurrent siblings can produce two.

finding: §4.2 fires last_failure on two distinct triggers — "a unit exits non-zero, or closes with a failed quality gate" — but only the first has a test (23) and only the first has an obvious writer. The gate branch cannot be written by the driver (§5.2 allows the harness's exit code not to carry the inner command's), so it must be written by `tp done` inside the child, from TP_UNIT_KIND/TP_UNIT_ID/TP_RUN_DIR; the spec never says so, never says what `exit_code` records in that case, and never says whether a gate failure inside a child that then exits 0 stops the run.
suggestion: Name the writer for each branch and the exit_code recorded for the gate branch, and extend test 23 with a failing-gate close whose harness exits 0.

finding: §5.2 says "a unit that needs a user-only decision runs `tp escalate`", but nothing routes a unit to that command. The four fenced operations exit 2 with "a hint naming it a user-approved decision" — the hint text is never said to mention `tp escalate`, and §3.2.1's `{prompt}` is only "run this unit's brief_command, do that one unit, stop". A fresh unattended process therefore hits a refusal with no documented instruction telling it the escalation path exists, and §8a.5 says a bare exit 2 is a stop-and-hand-to-a-human, so the escalation branch is unreachable in practice.
suggestion: State that under `TP_UNATTENDED` each fenced refusal's hint names `tp escalate --decision <name>` with the matching decision name, and/or that the driver's per-kind prompt carries the escalation affordance.

finding: `notify_cmd` is exec'd by the driver on every non-converged stop, and unlike every hook (§6.4, 10-second timeout, test 43) it is given no timeout and no bound of any kind. A notify_cmd that blocks strands the driver after the run has otherwise finished — past its wall-clock cap, with the run state already written — and §5.2's guarantee that "its exit code is reported and changes nothing" is untestable for a command that never exits. Test 42 pins the environment and the exit-code independence but not the hang.
suggestion: Give notify_cmd an explicit timeout with the value stated (the hooks' 10 seconds is the obvious precedent), define the recorded outcome on timeout, and add that case to test 42.

finding: Round 8 homed the version preflight in the SessionStart hook: "the check runs in the SessionStart hook (§6.2), which is the only hook that fires before a unit does any work". That scopes the guarantee to harnesses that load the plugin, while §6.3 explicitly contemplates the other case ("A runner that cannot load a plugin gets no agent definitions, and the unit runs without them") and §3.2.1 ships an opencode template that loads no Claude plugin. §6.1's promise that the plugin "fails with the install command rather than degrading quietly" therefore no longer holds on the very path the runner abstraction exists to support — an opencode run against a pre-0.35.0 tp degrades exactly as quietly as before.
suggestion: Say in §6.1 that the hook preflight covers plugin-loading harnesses only, and give the non-plugin path an equivalent: e.g. tp run itself refuses when the resolved tp binary the children will invoke is below the plugin minimum, or state the gap as accepted with its reason.

finding: §3.3 claims its predicates are what "lets the Stop hook (§6.2) and the driver's own success test read the same condition", but §6.2 defines the hook as firing when the unit has "neither its findings file nor an escalation record" and describes it as reading the two paths — an existence test. §3.3's predicate is existence plus every line parsing, and test 48 pins that a file with an unparseable line fails the predicate. A role unit that writes a malformed file therefore passes the Stop hook and fails the driver's check, so the two do not read the same condition after all.
suggestion: State in §6.2 that the Stop hook applies §3.3's full predicate for the -role kinds (file exists and every line parses), or drop §3.3's 'same condition' claim and say the hook is a cheaper existence pre-check the driver's predicate supersedes.

finding: §6.3 says tp-reviewer and tp-auditor "may write exactly one path — their own findings file at $TP_ROUND_DIR/$TP_UNIT_ID.ndjson — and are denied every other write." §5.2 requires that any unit needing a user-only decision run tp escalate, which writes a second path, $TP_RUN_DIR/$TP_UNIT_SEQ-escalation.json, and §6.2's Stop hook explicitly expects a role unit to be able to have produced that record. The allowlist as written fences off the escalation route for exactly the two kinds the Stop hook checks it for.
suggestion: Scope the sentence to the tool-level write matcher (§6.2's Write/Edit tools) and state that tp's own commands, including tp escalate, are unaffected — or list the escalation record as a second permitted path for the role agents.

finding: `notify_cmd` "is read from `.tp/local.json` only", but no command is given that writes it there. §5.1 fences `tp set --workflow notify_cmd=` under `TP_UNATTENDED`, which implies `tp set --workflow` is the setter outside it — yet `tp set --workflow` writes the task file's workflow override, a layer §7 says `notify_cmd` never reads. So the documented setter writes a layer the documented reader ignores, and the operator is left hand-editing a git-ignored file.
suggestion: Name the supported write path for `notify_cmd` — either a `tp config --local notify_cmd=…` form or an explicit statement that `tp set --workflow notify_cmd=` targets `.tp/local.json` for this field — and make §5.1's fence refer to that same path.

finding: `runner` is declared to resolve through the layered path CLI > env > task override > project config, and §5.1 refers to `TP_RUNNER` as "the fenced env layer of the `runner` field" — but `runner` can be a built-in name, an object, or a per-kind map, and the spec never says how a non-scalar value is encoded in the env layer or whether a CLI flag exists at all (no `--runner` appears in §3.5's flag list). Every other §7 field is a scalar, so there is no existing convention to inherit.
suggestion: State the encoding explicitly: `TP_RUNNER` (and any CLI flag) accepts a built-in template name only, or accepts a JSON document — and name the flag if one exists, or say the object and map shapes are config-file-only.

finding: §7 exempts notify_cmd from the project path ("per-operator rather than per-project and is read from .tp/local.json only") and then, four lines later, says tp config --resolved, tp config --extract and tp validate --project "cover the new fields on the same terms as every existing workflow field" — which for --extract means writing notify_cmd into the committed .tp/config.json, where by the first rule it can never be read. The spec also never names the command that WRITES notify_cmd into .tp/local.json; test 16 pins only that it is read from there.
suggestion: Say which of the three commands notify_cmd is excluded from (at minimum --extract, and whether --project errors when it appears in project config), and name the supported write path into .tp/local.json.

finding: §7's Range for `runner` is "Built-in name or object", but §3.2 says `runner` "takes one of three shapes: a built-in template name, a runner object, or a map from unit kind to either of those with a `default` key" and makes a map missing `default` a usage error. A test written against §7's table would reject the per-kind map that §3.2 requires, and the usage error for a `default`-less map is pinned in no test at all (tests 10-11 cover placeholders and spend only).
suggestion: Extend §7's Range cell to name all three shapes, and add a test asserting that a per-kind map resolves per kind and that a map without `default` exits 2.

finding: `location_clusters` entries are given as `{location, roles[], severities[], count}` with no semantics for the fields, so test 28 cannot be written the same way twice: is `count` the number of findings or the number of roles; is `severities[]` one entry per finding or a deduplicated set (and in what order); are clusters computed before or after the (location,class) dedup that §8a.1 says under-collapses; and is the key absent or `[]` when no location has two roles? The nil-vs-empty question matters most — an unattended driver branching on `location_clusters` sees `null` if the implementation uses a bare slice.
suggestion: Pin each field in one sentence (count = findings in the cluster; severities = deduplicated, in the documented severity order; clusters computed on the post-dedup set), state that the key is always present and `[]` when empty, and have test 28 assert the exact object for a two-role fixture.

finding: §8a.3 says auto-detect "caps its file set at 50" and adds `truncated`, but never says which side of 50 is truncated. At exactly 50 changed files, `truncated` may be reported true or false and both readings conform. Test 30 exercises only the truncated case, so nothing pins the untruncated invariant (`truncated` false and `total_changed == total_files`) either — the same blind spot CLAUDE.md records from v0.34.0, where a documented 1-60 range was "verified" with 999.
suggestion: State the rule as "truncated is true iff total_changed > 50" and extend test 30 with two boundary cases: exactly 50 files (truncated false, total_changed == total_files) and 51 files (truncated true).

finding: §8a.5 justifies moving every Args validator to exit 2 as "matching §9's definition of a usage error", but §9 is the Non-Goals list and contains no definition of a usage error or any exit-code semantics. The section that a reader must consult to check the change is therefore unidentified, and the invariant actually being appealed to (the 0/1/2/3/4 exit-code table) lives in skills/tp/REFERENCE.md, not in this spec.
suggestion: Cite the exit-code table in skills/tp/REFERENCE.md (or restate the definition inline in §8a.5) instead of §9, and check the other §-references added in §8a for the same drift.

finding: Test 18's first clause — "Each durable-write predicate is decidable from one file with no baseline" — is a property of the design, not an assertion a test can make; no fixture distinguishes a conforming implementation from one that consults two files. Only its second clause (an audit-fix closing a finding without a code change passes) is executable. The `review-resolve` predicate compounds this: "every finding in the round's file carries a disposition" names no JSON field, so even that predicate cannot be checked mechanically.
suggestion: Replace the first clause with the observable it stands for — e.g. "each predicate holds when evaluated against a fresh checkout of the single named file, with no prior state present" — and name the field `review-resolve` inspects.

finding: Tests 32 and 49 assert overlapping halves of §8a.4 after the round-8 blank-line carve-out: 32 already covers "exits 1 when an input has lines and none parsed" and "exits 0 when every input is zero-byte — for both merges", and 49 restates the exit-1 case for a single malformed line, adding only the blank-lines-only case. Two rows for one rule invite them to drift apart the way §10.6's entry count already did.
suggestion: Fold 49's blank-line case into 32 as a third clause and drop the separate row, or narrow 32 to the inputs payload and leave every exit-code assertion to 49.

finding: `{log_path}` is part of the public runner-template contract, but §3.5 already has the driver stream each child's output to that path, and neither built-in template (`claude`, `opencode`) uses the placeholder. Its only consumer is `TP_RUNNER_SEAM`'s fake runner, whose final spend line would reach the same file through the stream the driver already captures. Every operator writing a custom runner now has one more placeholder to read about and resolve for a channel the driver duplicates.
suggestion: Either drop `{log_path}` from §3.2's placeholder table and give the seam runner args `["{unit_kind}", "{unit_id}", "{max_budget_usd}"]` with its spend line on stdout, or state in §3.2.1 which real runner needs the path as an argument and why the driver's own stream does not serve it.

finding: `tp run --status` is defined only for "the current or last run". The case with no `.tp/run-<base>.json` — a repo where `tp run` has never been invoked, or one where the file was deleted — has no defined output or exit code, and it is the first thing an operator or a monitoring script hits.
suggestion: State the empty case: `tp run --status` with no run state exits 0 with a payload whose `run_state` is null (or exits 3 with a hint), and say which.

finding: `file_summary` gains two new keys where one carries the information: `truncated` is exactly `total_changed > total_files` in every case the section describes, so the boolean is a projection of two numbers emitted in the same object and feeds no decision a consumer cannot make from them. The stated justification ("The flag is in the payload, so `--quiet` cannot erase it") applies to `total_changed` alone and does not earn the second key.
suggestion: Emit `total_changed` next to `total_files` and drop `truncated`; state in §8a.3 that a consumer detects truncation as `total_changed > total_files`. Amend test 30 to assert the two counts rather than the flag.
